headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via OpenMetadata MCP/webhook surfaces; Taipy’s local-only network posture limits leakage but not workflow confusion.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, events, and webhooks, so it can ingest external content that Taipy may later consume in workflows. Taipy has no documented input isolation or provenance controls here, so a prompt-injection bridge is plausible, though not proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes OpenMetadata-generated text or webhook payloads as instructions
IF OpenMetadata MCP or webhook content is forwarded into Taipy without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata webhooks into Taipy
Add a provenance tag to all OpenMetadata-derived text before Taipy reads it
Require manual review for any Taipy action triggered by catalog metadata
Restrict OpenMetadata MCP tools to read-only operations
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data classes, while Taipy documents no data classes touched and advertises network egress none. With no shared workspace or upload path documented, leakage is not evidenced; the main risk is limited to accidental local exposure if operators bridge outputs manually.
conditions: IF operators place sensitive OpenMetadata exports into a shared folder readable by Taipy
IF Taipy is configured to read local files containing OpenMetadata metadata
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata exports in a separate directory
Do not mount a shared workspace between the agents
Review Taipy file inputs before execution
Redact governance and lineage fields before transfer
requires-engineering: add access controls on any shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and can write through APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks; Taipy’s concurrency model is unspecified and its network egress is none. There is no documented shared mutable resource or locking conflict, so only a limited coordination risk exists if both are pointed at the same files or state.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same local files or database tables
IF Taipy is given write access to OpenMetadata-managed state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same dataset or config files
Serialize any shared-state updates manually
Check for file locks before running write operations
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit metadata, lineage, and governance outputs that Taipy could treat as inputs for dashboards or automation. Taipy is a job-scheduler/data-integration tool, so if it acts on those outputs without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Taipy schedules jobs based on OpenMetadata outputs without validation
IF OpenMetadata metadata errors are propagated into Taipy workflows
mitigations: Insert a validation step between OpenMetadata and Taipy
Require human approval for downstream actions
Compare OpenMetadata outputs against source systems before use
Log and alert on schema or lineage mismatches
requires-engineering: build typed contracts between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata clearly handles governance, lineage, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include regulated metadata, while Taipy’s docs here do not show a specific residency or retention mismatch. Because no direct compliance conflict is documented, the risk is limited to operator-created policy gaps rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated metadata is exported from OpenMetadata into Taipy-managed storage
IF Taipy retention or logging differs from the source policy
mitigations: Classify data before moving it into Taipy
Align retention settings across both systems
Avoid storing regulated fields in Taipy logs
Review residency requirements for any shared dataset
requires-engineering: document a joint data-handling policy
